title: Experimentation Audit: Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) in Checkout A/B Test
problem_brief: The Growth team is celebrating an A/B test of the checkout flow showing Variant B has a +14.2% lift in average order value (AOV) with p < 0.01. However, looking at the sample allocation count shows Control received 54,200 users while Variant B received only 45,800 users (54.2% vs 45.8%), despite configuring a 50/50 split. Perform a Chi-Square goodness-of-fit test for Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM), investigate the redirect loop telemetry, and advise leadership on whether to ship.

entries.message: Safari iOS: 302 redirect loop detected (3 redirects). Safari dropped session cookie and fell back to Control
High-value desktop Chrome users successfully entered Variant B; mobile Safari users dropped back to Control

submission_fields.label: 1. Executive Summary & SRM Verdict
submission_fields.placeholder: State clearly whether Variant B's +14.2% lift is valid or an invalid artifact of selection bias...
submission_fields.guidance: Explain why an experiment with p < 0.00001 SRM is fundamentally compromised.

submission_fields.label: 2. Chi-Square Goodness of Fit & Survivorship Bias Analysis
submission_fields.placeholder: Calculate and explain the Chi-Square metric and how mobile Safari users were systematically filtered...
submission_fields.guidance: Demonstrate that Variant B only measured affluent desktop users while mobile dropped out.

submission_fields.label: 3. Immediate Decision for Leadership
submission_fields.placeholder: Should leadership launch Variant B or declare the test invalid and abort?
submission_fields.guidance: Explain the business cost of deploying an unrepresentative variant.

submission_fields.label: 4. Experimentation Integrity Guardrails
submission_fields.placeholder: What automated SRM checks and edge-worker routing tests should be added to future A/B tests?
submission_fields.guidance: Propose daily automated SRM alerting and server-side feature flagging.

dimensions.name: Statistical Understanding of SRM
dimensions.criteria: Identifies Chi^2 = 70.56 (p < 0.0001) as severe Sample Ratio Mismatch proving experimental randomization failed.

dimensions.name: Survivorship Bias & Root Cause Identification
dimensions.criteria: Explains how the Safari redirect loop filtered out mobile traffic, creating artificial selection bias that inflated AOV in Variant B.

dimensions.name: Executive Guidance & Decision Integrity
dimensions.criteria: Firmly recommends DO NOT SHIP Variant B, halting premature celebration and saving the company from unexpected conversion drops.

dimensions.name: Automated Experimentation Guardrails
dimensions.criteria: Proposes automated daily Chi-Square SRM checks in the experimentation dashboard that auto-pause compromised experiments.
